equation_request.abstract: Ab initio computation of molecular properties is one of the most promising applications of quantum computing. While this problem is widely believed to be intractable for classical computers, efficient quantum algorithms exist which have the potential to vastly accelerate research throughput in fields ranging from material science to drug discovery. Using a solid-state quantum register realized in a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) defect in diamond, we compute the bond dissociation curve of the minimal basis helium hydride cation, HeH+. Moreover, we report an energy uncertainty (given our model basis) of the order of $10^{-14}$ Hartree, which is ten orders of magnitude below desired chemical precision. As NV centers in diamond provide a robust and straightforward platform for quantum information processing, our work provides several important steps towards a fully scalable solid state implementation of a quantum chemistry simulator.

specification.problem: Compute the ground-state energy of minimal-basis HeH+ as a function of bond length (dissociation curve) on a two-qubit solid-state NV-center register, via phase estimation-type energy extraction. The abstract gives no circuit details.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest construction: a generic 2-qubit qubit-encoded Hamiltonian for minimal-basis HeH+ at a single bond length, with an iterative phase-estimation-style energy readout. The specific Hamiltonian coefficients, NV control sequences, the paper's actual algorithm, and the 1e-14 Hartree uncertainty analysis are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: qubit Hamiltonian of HeH+ in minimal basis at bond length R
real Pauli coefficients (not given in abstract)

equations.label: Qubit Hamiltonian
equations.description: Pauli decomposition of the molecular Hamiltonian after fermion-to-qubit mapping and reduction to 2 qubits.
equations.justification: Abstract only says minimal basis HeH+; a 2-qubit Pauli form is a proposed standard construction and the register size is assumed.
assumptions: coefficients g_i(R) from a classical electronic-structure calculation, not given

equations.label: Ground-state energy
equations.description: Target quantity at each R; the dissociation curve is E_0(R) over a grid of R (plus nuclear repulsion if not included in H).
equations.abstract_quote: we compute the bond dissociation curve of the minimal basis helium hydride cation, HeH+
equations.justification: A dissociation curve is the ground-state energy versus bond length; the variational form is the standard definition.
assumptions: nuclear repulsion energy included in H or added classically

equations.label: Time evolution
equations.description: Unitary whose eigenphase encodes the energy.
equations.justification: Standard phase-estimation setup; the abstract does not state that this method was used.
assumptions: Trotterization or exact compilation to NV gates not specified

equations.label: Phase-energy relation
equations.description: Energy read from the eigenphase, defined modulo 2π/τ, so τ must be chosen to avoid aliasing.
equations.justification: Standard phase estimation relation; the sign convention and the 2π factor depend on the definition of φ.
assumptions: |ψ0> is an eigenstate (ground state) or has large overlap with it

equations.label: Uncertainty statement
equations.description: Reported energy uncertainty within the model basis, far below chemical precision of about 1.6e-3 Hartree.
equations.abstract_quote: we report an energy uncertainty (given our model basis) of the order of $10^{-14}$ Hartree
equations.justification: Stated in the abstract; its derivation is not given.

registers.name: system
registers.role: encodes the HeH+ minimal-basis electronic state

registers.name: ancilla
registers.role: phase-estimation readout qubit; in an NV system this could be an electron or nuclear spin, but this is not stated

specification.initial_state: Assumed: Hartree-Fock-like reference product state on the system register, ancilla in |+>.

steps.description: Classically compute g_i(R) for the chosen R and build the 2-qubit Hamiltonian.
Prepare the reference state on the system register and the ancilla in superposition.
Apply controlled-U(τ) for chosen τ values.
Measure the ancilla and estimate the phase.
Convert the phase to the energy and repeat over a grid of R to obtain the curve.

specification.measurement: Assumed: ancilla measured in the X/Y basis to estimate the phase.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Convert the phase to energy, resolve aliasing, and assemble E_0(R) over R.
assumptions: The algorithm is assumed to be phase-estimation-like; the abstract does not specify it.
The register is assumed to be 2 system qubits plus 1 ancilla.
Coefficients, orbitals and basis details are not given.
missing_information: NV spin assignment and pulse sequences
Origin and definition of the 1e-14 Hartree uncertainty
